{"replace_all": false, "file_path": "/Users/brvu/workspace/poc_ai/ai-code-review-arena/debate-review/README.md", "old_string": "## Why this exists

A single model is a single point of view. In a structured benchmark on real
bug-introducing PRs, the **best individual model caught ~53% of known bugs** —
but when several models **debated** each other for a few rounds, detection rose
to **~80%**, and the hardest system-level bugs hit **100%**. The gain doesn't
come from one model being smarter; it comes from models having **different blind
spots**. One walks the call chain; another is terse but catches the one
off-by-one everyone missed. Debate forces each to defend or revise its claims
against the others.

`debate-review` packages that workflow into a single command you can run on your
own branches before opening or merging a PR:", "new_string": "## Why I built this

A single model is a single point of view, and I kept getting contradictory
reviews — one model would flag a data race, another would call the same code
clean. So I stopped trusting any one model and started making them argue.

The gain isn't from one model being smarter; it's that models have **different
blind spots**. One walks the call chain and lives in the boring error paths;
another is terse but catches the one off-by-one everyone else skimmed past.
Forcing them to defend or revise their claims against each other — with every
point grounded in actual code — surfaces far more than running any of them
alone, and the things multiple models independently agree on are the things
worth acting on first.

`debate-review` is my opinionated take on that workflow: one command you run on
your own branches before opening or merging a PR."}
